existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `MedicinalProductIndication` is removed/merged in R6; the indication use case maps to `ClinicalUseDefinition` with `type="indication"`. The top migration concerns are resource identity/API breakage, mandatory type/subject plus path moves, and datatype/reference changes for subject, duration, undesirable effects, other therapy, and population. Confidence is medium-high for the structural break, but medium overall because no official ConceptMap or narrative migration rationale was available.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: The migration pattern is: create `ClinicalUseDefinition`; set `type` to `indication`; ensure a `subject`; move indication fields into `indication`; convert simple concepts to `CodeableReference.concept`; migrate old resource references to R6 definition resources; materialize populations as `Group`; and preserve R6-only status/applicability/library data with extensions or companion resources when down-converting.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the same-name R6 artifact is absent and that `ClinicalUseDefinition` is the appropriate R6 indication model, based on local StructureDefinitions, package indexes, and the R6 old-types CodeSystem. Confidence is lower for exact migration semantics because the local inputs did not include official diffs, ConceptMaps, StructureMaps, narrative ballot rationale, or terminology expansions.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
MedicinalProductIndication has a resource-identity break: MedicinalProductIndication is absent in R6 and its indication use case moved to ClinicalUseDefinition. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before element-level compatibility can solve much.

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 97/100, producing migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`.

9 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Prioritize an explicit migration map, successor-resource guidance, endpoint/search transition guidance, and compatibility profiles or aliases where they are cheap. Do not rely on preserving individual old element names to solve the main break.

topFindings.title: MedicinalProductIndication is absent in R6 and its indication use case moved to ClinicalUseDefinition
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance with `resourceType: MedicinalProductIndication` is not an R6 core resource and code using the old REST/type identity must migrate.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: undesirableEffect changed from Reference(MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect) to inline ClinicalUseDefinition undesirable-effect content
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a Reference to a standalone undesirable-effect resource is not valid in the R6 inline element; R6-to-R4 conversion may also require minting resource identities.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: duration changed from Quantity to duration[x] with Range or string, removing direct Quantity representation
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 Quantity duration cannot be copied into the R6 duration choice without choosing a lossy or convention-dependent representation.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: population changed from inline Population datatype to Reference(Group)
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: inline R4 Population objects cannot be used where R6 requires a Reference(Group), and R6-to-R4 conversion may lose Group identity or detailed criteria.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: otherTherapy child elements were renamed and the therapy target changed to CodeableReference
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 child names such as `therapyRelationshipType` and `medicationReference` are not valid R6 names, and legacy product/substance targets need migration.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Indication-specific data moved from resource-level fields into ClinicalUseDefinition.indication
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: old generated properties and path expressions no longer point at valid R6 content; raw old top-level fields are not valid under the R6 replacement.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 indication representation requires an explicit type code and at least one subject
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 indication with no subject cannot satisfy R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition.subject` minimum, and a transform must synthesize `type = indication`.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: subject changed from Reference(MedicinalProduct|Medication) to mandatory CodeableReference with different target set
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 references to `MedicinalProduct` are not valid R6 subject targets without target-resource migration; R6 code-only or newly targeted subjects also lose information when mapped back to R4.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 replacement adds optional identifier/category/status/applicability/library fields, including modifier status, with no R4 base slots
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 instances using status, applicability, or library cannot be faithfully represented in base R4, but no old R4-valid instance is rejected because these fields were added.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
